name: ROSEN
description: Concurred with majority opinion

name: STANDRIDGE
description: Concurred with majority opinion

name: Wall, J
description: Concurred, argued that Stubbs had standing to bring a facial challenge to the statute, but the statute was not unconstitutionally vague and his convictions were supported by sufficient evidence.

name: Biles, J
description: Concurred in denying relief but dissented from the majority's path, arguing it uproots precedent by allowing a facial challenge to a statute that clearly prohibited Stubbs' conduct.

name: Standridge, J
description: Concurred that the evidence challenge failed but dissented from the majority's decision to depart from vagueness precedent, arguing it ignores prudential standing rules and opens the door to abstract litigation.

name: Stegall, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Kansas Constitution grants judicial power only to actual controversies, and once a case is moot, jurisdiction is extinguished, thus overruling prior caselaw on "prudential exceptions."

name: Biles, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision to eliminate "prudential exceptions" to mootness is not constitutionally compelled and will allow rights violations to escape judicial review, harming ordinary Kansans.

name: Rosen, J.
description: Dissented, joined Justice Biles' dissenting opinion.

name: Standridge, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's rigid interpretation of mootness departs from historical precedent and that the Kansas Constitution allows for a flexible application of mootness doctrine, including prudential exceptions.

name: Biles, J.
description: Concurred in the result but dissented from the majority's standing analysis regarding State v. Stubbs.

name: Standridge, J.
description: Concurred in the result but argued that Green's vagueness challenge to the premeditated first-degree murder statute should be examined as an as-applied judicial review, not a facial challenge, under the federal vagueness doctrine.

name: Marla Luckert
description: Denied the petition for review, allowing the Court of Appeals' decision to stand.

name: STANDRIDGE, J.
description: Concurred, delivering the opinion that the Challenged Laws infringed on the fundamental right to abortion and failed strict scrutiny.

name: WALL, J.
description: Did not participate.

name: ROSEN, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that the court's decision in Hodes I, which held personal autonomy as a fundamental right subject to strict scrutiny, was correctly applied and not changed by the current ruling.

name: BILES, J.
description: Concurred, fully agreeing with the majority's analysis and result, and clarified his previous concurrence regarding the application of strict scrutiny.

name: WILSON, J.
description: Concurred, agreeing the regulations impermissibly burdened the right to abortion, but expressed concerns about the majority's reasoning potentially changing the Hodes I holding.

name: STEGALL, J.
description: Dissented, arguing the majority's decision effectively overruled Hodes I by changing the definition of fundamental rights, leading to unrestricted abortion access and undermining the regulatory state.

name: STEGALL, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: ROSEN, J.
description: Concurred in part and Dissented in part, argued that the majority misstates state law, ignores key aspects of the plaintiffs' case, and endangers basic voting rights by nullifying Section 2's protection of the right to vote and incorrectly analyzing other election laws.

name: BILES, J.
description: Concurred in part and Dissented in part, argued that the majority's opinion misstates state law and endangers the fundamental right to vote by rejecting otherwise lawful ballots based on subjective signature verification and by nullifying Section 2's protection of the right to vote.

name: STANDRIDGE, J.
description: Concurred in part and Dissented in part, argued that the majority wrongly holds Section 2 of the Kansas Constitution Bill of Rights does not protect the right to vote, departing from long-standing precedent and undermining democratic principles.

name: Rosen, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that an elected governing body cannot use its legislative power to bind future governing bodies to general policy decisions, as this would frustrate the will of the electorate.

name: STEGALL, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the reapportionment legislation is valid as it comports with procedural requirements for lawmaking and substantive constitutional and statutory requirements, including the "one person one vote" standard and the Voting Rights Act, and found no evidence of invidious discrimination or political gerrymandering.

name: Stegall, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the plaintiffs failed to prove that the Ad Astra 2 map violated the Kansas Constitution regarding partisan or racial gerrymandering and that partisan gerrymandering claims are nonjusticiable without codified standards.

name: Rosen, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision gives a stamp of approval to an assault on the democratic system, ignores the plain language of the state's Constitution, and distorts legal reasoning to uphold racial discrimination and political chicanery, further arguing that Section 2 of the Kansas Constitution Bill of Rights provides broader protections than the Fourteenth Amendment.

name: Biles, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Ad Astra 2 legislation intentionally targets Kansans based on voting history, political views, and race, and that the district court's factual findings support that the map is an unconstitutional partisan and racial gerrymander, and that the Kansas Constitution provides manageable standards for judicial review of such claims.

name: Standridge, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Ad Astra 2 map violates plaintiffs' right to equal protection by intentionally diluting voting strength and using race as a motivating factor, and that the majority's decision undermines democratic norms and constitutional protections.

name: Wall, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that the natural right to life is forfeitable, not absolute, and the state's capital sentencing scheme does not infringe upon this right.

name: Biles, J.
description: Concurred with the majority result and rationale, but found much of the majority's Section 1 analysis unnecessary, believing the issue was effectively disposed of by prior precedent.

name: Stegall, J.
description: Concurred with the decision to affirm the death sentence but expressed deep doubts and reluctance, arguing that the court's Section 1 jurisprudence (from Hodes) is a gross constitutional error that magnifies state power and strips citizens of substantive rights.

name: Luckert, C.J.
description: Dissented from the majority's determination that cumulative errors did not affect the jury verdict, arguing that the numerous interlocking errors in the trial made it impossible to eliminate the possibility that at least one juror would have decided mitigating factors or mercy outweighed aggravating factors.

name: Wall, J.
description: Concurred, affirming the death sentence and finding no entitlement to relief on penalty-phase issues.

name: Biles, J.
description: Concurred with the majority result and rationale, with one exception as explained in his separate concurrence in a companion case.

name: Stegall, J.
description: Concurred with the majority's decision to affirm, but expressed deep doubts and reluctance, dissenting from the court's Section 1 jurisprudence which he views as a gross constitutional error that magnifies state power.

name: Luckert, C.J.
description: Dissented, arguing that the cumulative effect of many errors likely affected the jury's verdict, making the death sentence unreliable.

name: Wall, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that Brown failed to prove intentional discrimination in peremptory challenges, the KSGA does not violate Section 5, and the restitution order is constitutionally firm after severing unconstitutional provisions, but agreed to remand for resentencing due to an illegal classification of a prior juvenile adjudication.

name: Standridge, J.
description: Dissented, arguing against the majority's analysis and conclusion on the issue of restitution.

name: Rosen, J.
description: Dissented, joining Judge Standridge's opinion on the restitution issue.

name: Wilson, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while the restitution order against Arnett was affirmed, the statutes allowing criminal restitution to be enforced as civil judgments without a jury trial violate the Kansas Constitution Bill of Rights and should be severed.

name: Standridge, J.
description: Dissented, argued that Kansas' restitution statutes violate both the Sixth Amendment and section 5 of the Kansas Constitution Bill of Rights, and Arnett should have had a jury determine the amount of damage or loss.

name: Rosen, J.
description: Dissented, argued that Kansas' criminal restitution statutes unconstitutionally deprived Arnett of her section 5 right to have a jury determine whether her crime caused damage or loss.

name: Wilson, J.
description: Concurred, argued that severing the problematic statutory language that made criminal restitution orders equivalent to civil judgments preserves the societal goals of restitution without infringing on a defendant's right to a jury trial.

name: Standridge, J.
description: Not participating.

name: Rosen, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Kansas criminal restitution statutes are unconstitutional because they allow a judge, rather than a jury, to determine restitution amounts, and would have vacated the restitution order.

name: Wall, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the KSGA's method of determining a defendant's criminal history does not implicate section 5's right to trial by jury, as the court's role is to determine punishment and the jury's role is to determine guilt or innocence.

name: Biles, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the wrongful birth tort was a new cause of action created in 1990, not a common-law right existing at the time the Kansas Constitution was adopted, and therefore the statute abolishing it is constitutional.

name: Beier, J.
description: Not participating.

name: Michael E. Ward
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: Stegall, J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that Arche v. United States should be overruled for legalizing discrimination against disabled children, and that wrongful birth is not a "new" tort but a traditional negligence action.

name: Luckert, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that the statute is unconstitutional because wrongful birth is a form of medical malpractice, a common-law action protected by the Kansas Constitution's right to a jury trial.

name: Rosen, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the statute is unconstitutional as it infringes on personal autonomy and the right to make informed decisions about pregnancy, and questioned the majority's test for constitutional validity.
